Mastering API Architecture, poora — ek hi jagah.

Ye SPA Mastering API Architecture (O'Reilly, 289 pages, 10 chapters) ki poori book ko ek hi page me samjhata hai — Hinglish me. API design karna, test karna, gateway aur service mesh lagana, deploy/release karna, threat modeling aur OAuth2 se secure karna, aur purane monolith ko API-driven architecture me badalna — sab kuch, ek hi jagah, ek hi case study (conference system + Attendee API) ke saath.

49Sections
10Chapters
16Book figures
8Interactive labs
36Interview FAQs

Kaise padho

  • Part I (Ch 1–2): API design karo aur test karo — REST, RPC, GraphQL, OpenAPI, versioning, contract testing.
  • Part II (Ch 3–4): Traffic manage karo — API gateway (north–south) aur service mesh (east–west).
  • Part III (Ch 5–7): Operate aur secure karo — deploy/release, threat modeling, OAuth2/JWT.
  • Part IV (Ch 8–10): Evolve karo — monolith se API-driven architecture, cloud migration, future.

Har section ke ant me Source line hai (kis chapter se liya gaya). Beech-beech me 8 interactive labs hain — haath se try karo. Aakhir me Interview FAQs aur Trust Check hai, jo gin ke batata hai ki sab kuch cover hai ya nahi.

Case study — conference system

Poori book ek hi case study par chalti hai: ek conference system jisme Attendee API hai. Pehle ye monolith ke andar tha, phir use alag service ke roop me nikala gaya, gateway se expose kiya, mesh se connect kiya, aur ant me cloud me le jaaya gaya. Har chapter me yahi Attendee API aage badhta hai — isliye concepts ek-doosre se judte hain, alag-alag nahi lagte.

01.1Part I · Design, Build, Test

Case Study: Attendee API — conference system

Book ek conference system se shuru hoti hai. Ek purana (legacy) monolith hai jo conference chalata hai — sessions, bookings, attendees sab ek hi code base me. Ab ek naya Attendee API banana hai jo attendees ko manage kare, aur use pehle legacy system se, phir mobile app se, phir bahari (external) systems se connect karna hai.

Attendee API kya karta hai

  • Attendees ko list karna: GET /attendees — saare attendees ki list.
  • Ek attendee ko dekhna: GET /attendees/{id} — ek khaas attendee ki details.
  • Naya attendee banana: POST /attendees — naya attendee create karo, 201 Created aur Location header ke saath.
  • Attendee hatana: DELETE /attendees/{id}.

Do consumers, do alag zarooratein

  • CFP (Call for Papers) team — ye internal consumer hai. Use clean, loosely coupled REST model chahiye taaki wo aasani se integrate kar sake.
  • Legacy conference team — ye purana monolith hai. Iske liye REST bhi chalega, lekin RPC bhi ek option hai kyunki performance aur direct method call yahan zyada matter karta hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: API design karne se pehle consumer ko samjho. Consumer kaun hai, use kya chahiye, aur wo kis tarah integrate karega — ye decide karega ki REST lo, RPC lo, ya GraphQL lo. Technology pehle nahi, consumer pehle.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 1
01.2Part I · Design, Build, Test

REST by example — HTTP, stateless, representations

REST (Representational State Transfer) ka matlab hai: tum resources ko HTTP ke zariye expose karte ho, aur har request me poora context bhejta hai — server client ki state yaad nahi rakhta. Ye stateless hona REST ki sabse badi taakat hai.

Ek REST exchange kaisa dikhta hai

GET http://mastering-api.com/attendees
Accept: application/json
---
200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "displayName": "[Name]",
  "id": 1
}
  • Request line: method (GET) + URL (resource ka address).
  • Accept header: consumer batata hai use kis format me data chahiye (application/json).
  • Status code: 200 OK ka matlab request successfully process hui.
  • Representation: body me resource ka ek representation (yahan JSON) — resource khud nahi, uska ek roop.

Stateless ka matlab

Server client ki koi state yaad nahi rakhta. Agar tumhe /attendees/1 ki details chahiye, toh har request me poora context bhejna padta hai. Isse server ko scale karna aasan ho jaata hai — koi bhi server instance koi bhi request handle kar sakta hai, kyunki use pehle wali request ki yaad nahi chahiye.

Content type soch-samajh ke chuno

JSON sabse common hai kyunki har system use parse kar sakta hai. application/pdf return karna bhi valid hai, lekin use koi doosra system aasani se use nahi kar payega. Content type wahi chuno jo consumer aasani se parse kar sake.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 1
01.3Part I · Design, Build, Test

Richardson Maturity Model — Level 0 se Level 3

Leonard Richardson ne 2008 me QCon me bataya ki REST APIs alag-alag levels par bante hain. Ye model batata hai ki tumhari API kitni "RESTful" hai. Level 2 tak pahunchna aksar kaafi hota hai — Level 3 har jagah zaroori nahi.

LevelNaamMatlabExample
0HTTP / RPCSirf ek URI, HTTP use kar rahe ho, lekin resource ka model nahi hai. Ye asal me RPC hai jo HTTP par chal raha hai.POST /attendees (sab kuch ek endpoint se)
1ResourcesResources ko URI me model karna shuru. Har cheez ki apni identity hai.GET /attendees/1 (ek khaas attendee)
2Verbs (Methods)Sahi HTTP methods use karo — GET state change nahi karta, PUT/DELETE alag kaam karte hain. Ek hi URI par alag methods, alag operations.GET /attendees/1, PUT /attendees/1, DELETE /attendees/1
3Hypermedia Controls (HATEOAS)Response me hi bataya jaata hai ki aage kya actions possible hain — API navigable ban jaati hai.GET /attendees/1 ke response me "update" aur "delete" ke links

Level 2 kyun kaafi hai

Level 2 par tum ek samajh me aane wala resource model dikhate ho, sahi actions ke saath. Isse coupling kam hoti hai aur backend ki poori detail chhup jaati hai. Level 3 (HATEOAS) practical terms me modern REST services me rarely use hota hai — ye chatty hota hai (har step par nayi request) aur inter-service calls ke liye suit nahi karta. UI-style systems me navigation ka fayda hai, lekin service-to-service me pehle se poori specification hona zyada behtar hai.

Interview me: "Richardson Maturity Model kya hai?" — Level 0 (single URI, RPC over HTTP), Level 1 (resources with identity), Level 2 (correct HTTP verbs), Level 3 (HATEOAS/hypermedia). Aur ye bhi batao ki Level 2 aksar practical target hai, Level 3 har jagah zaroori nahi.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 1
01.4Part I · Design, Build, Test

RPC APIs aur gRPC — direct method call

RPC (Remote Procedure Call) me tum ek process me method call karte ho, lekin wo code doosre process me execute hota hai. REST ek resource model dikhata hai; RPC ek method ko directly expose karta hai. gRPC aaj ka de facto standard hai RPC ke liye.

Figure 1-1. Example C4 component diagram using gRPC

gRPC kaise kaam karta hai

  • Server: Attendee service ek gRPC server start karta hai ek port par, aur apne methods ko remotely callable banata hai.
  • Client (stub): Legacy conference service ek stub use karta hai — ek library jo remote call ki complexity ko chhupa deti hai. Tum local method call karte ho, stub use network call me badal deta hai.
  • Schema: gRPC ko poora interaction cover karne ke liye ek schema chahiye (Protocol Buffers). Bina schema ke producer aur consumer ek-doosre ko samajh nahi sakte.

REST vs RPC — state ka farak

  • REST stateless hota hai — har request independent hai.
  • RPC me state implementation par depend karta hai — kuch RPC integrations exchange ke dauraan state bana lete hain. Isse performance badhti hai, lekin reliability aur routing complexity bhi badh sakti hai.
  • Coupling: RPC me model exact functionality batata hai jo doosri service se chahiye — isse coupling zyada ho sakti hai. Lekin coupling hamesha buri nahi hoti, khaas taur par east–west services me jahan performance key hai.

Kab RPC chuno

Jab tumhe internal service-to-service communication me high performance chahiye, aur tumhe exact method-level functionality chahiye, toh RPC (gRPC) achha option hai. Jab tumhe external consumers ko ek clean, loosely coupled resource model dikhana hai, toh REST behtar hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 1
01.5Part I · Design, Build, Test

GraphQL — ek query, kayi sources

GraphQL ek technology layer hai jo existing services, datastores aur APIs ke upar baithta hai aur ek query language deta hai. Client exactly wahi fields maang sakta hai jo use chahiye — na zyada, na kam — chahe wo fields kayi alag APIs me hon.

GraphQL kab chamakta hai

  • Mobile apps: Mobile devices ki screen chhoti aur network limited hota hai. REST me tumhe poora response milta hai, chahe tumhe sirf 2 fields chahiye hon. GraphQL me tum sirf wahi fields maango jo chahiye.
  • Kayi interconnected services: Jab data kayi subsystems me bikhra ho, GraphQL ek single version de sakta hai saari APIs par — consumer ko alag-alag version manage nahi karna padta.
  • UI aur reporting: UI modeling aur data warehousing-style systems ke liye GraphQL ideal hai kyunki tum exactly wahi data le sakte ho jo UI ko chahiye.

GraphQL ek facade bhi ho sakta hai

GraphQL ko existing legacy systems ke upar rakh kar unki complexity ko chhupaya ja sakta hai. Lekin agar tumhare paas pehle se well-designed APIs hain, toh unke upar GraphQL lagana aur bhi simple hota hai. GraphQL ko complementary technology samjho — ye REST/RPC ki jagah nahi leta, unke saath kaam karta hai.

Yaad rakho: REST ek resource model deta hai (ek API), RPC individual functions deta hai, GraphQL ek query language deta hai jo kayi sources ko jodta hai. Teeno ka apna use hai — scenario dekh ke chuno.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 1
01.6Part I · Design, Build, Test

REST standards — Microsoft guidelines, PII, naming

REST ke basic rules bahut simple hain, lekin implementation developer par chhod diya gaya hai. Error kaise dikhaye? Pagination kaise kare? Compatibility kaise na toote? Isliye standards/guidelines zaroori hain. Book Microsoft REST API Guidelines use karti hai (open source).

RFC-2119 — MUST, SHOULD, MUST NOT

Guidelines RFC-2119 ki terminology use karti hain: MUST (zaroori hai), SHOULD (karna chahiye), SHOULD NOT / MUST NOT (nahi karna chahiye). Isse developer ko pata chalta hai ki kya mandatory hai aur kya optional.

PII ko URL me mat daalo

Microsoft guidelines (section 7.9) kehte hain: personally identifiable information (PII) URL ka hissa nahi hona chahiye. Kyunki URL paths ya query parameters galti se cache ho sakte hain — server logs me, network me, kahin bhi. Email ko unique ID ke roop me URL me use mat karo; alag se ek opaque ID use karo.

POST http://mastering-api.com/attendees
{
  "displayName": "[Name]",
  "givenName": "[Name]",
  "surname": "[Name]",
  "email": "[Name]@example.com"
}
-- 201 CREATED
Location: http://mastering-api.com/attendees/1

Location header batata hai ki naya resource kahan banaya gaya. ID opaque hai (sirf 1), email URL me nahi hai.

Naming — domain data dictionary banao

Naam badalna bhi compatibility tod sakta hai (versioning me dekhenge). Standards me kuch standard names hote hain, lekin har team ko apna domain data dictionary bhi banana chahiye — common terminology jo saari APIs me consistent ho. Jo companies saari APIs me consistency rakhti hain, unke consumers ko samajhna aur connect karna aasan hota hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 1
01.7Part I · Design, Build, Test

Collections, pagination aur filtering

Jab tum GET /attendees karte ho, toh response me raw array dena tempting hai. Lekin behtar hai array ko ek object ke andar nest karna — isse tum pagination aur aage ki features add kar sakte ho bina compatibility tode.

Pagination kyun zaroori hai

Pagination ka matlab hai: poora result ek baar me mat do, partial result do aur batayo ki agla set kaise maange. Agar tum pehle raw array dete ho aur baad me pagination add karna chaho, toh array ko object me badalna padega — aur ye breaking change hoga.

GET http://mastering-api.com/attendees
-- 200 OK
{
  "value": [
    { "displayName": "[Name]", "id": 1 }
  ],
  "@nextLink": "{opaqueUrl}"
}

@nextLink ek opaque URL hai jo agle page ka address deta hai. Consumer ko ye samajhne ki zaroorat nahi ki pagination kaise kaam karta hai — bas @nextLink ko follow karo.

Filtering — OData $filter

Jab collections badi ho jaayein, toh filtering chahiye hoti hai. OData standard par based ek expression language hai:

GET http://mastering-api.com/attendees?$filter=displayName eq '[Name]'

Shuru se saari filtering features banana zaroori nahi hai. Lekin standards ke hisaab se design karoge, toh baad me filtering add kar sakte ho bina compatibility tode. (GraphQL filtering/querying me khaas taur par achha hai, khaas taur par jab kayi services me query karni ho.)

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 1
01.8Part I · Design, Build, Test

Error handling — status codes aur InnerError

Error handling wo cheez hai jo aksar baad me sochi jaati hai, lekin use pehle se define karna chahiye. Consumer ko exactly pata hona chahiye ki kya galat hua — isse support kam padta hai aur consumer apna code status code ke around likh sakta hai.

Status codes ka matlab

RangeMatlabConsumer kya kare
2xxSuccessRequest process hui. Galti se bhi error ko 2xx ke saath body me mat bhejo — consumer samjhega ki sab theek hai.
3xxRedirectKuch client libraries redirects ko automatically follow karti hain.
4xxClient-side errorRequest me kuch galat hai. message field yahan bahut useful hoti hai developer/end user ke liye.
5xxServer-side failureServer me problem hai. Kuch client libraries 5xx par retry karti hain.

Do's and Don'ts

  • Ek consistent error format rakho — guidelines kehte hain "developers SHOULD be able to write one piece of code that handles errors consistently."
  • Stack traces bahar mat bhejo — error messages me stack trace ya sensitive info mat do; ye hacker ki madad kar sakti hai.
  • InnerError use karo — Microsoft guidelines me InnerError ka concept hai jisme detailed stack trace/description rakh sakte ho debugging ke liye, lekin external consumer ko bhejne se pehle use strip kar do.
  • Unexpected failure socho — jaise payment system me agar 500 aaye, toh kya payment ho gaya ya nahi? Ye document karo.
SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 1
01.9Part I · Design, Build, Test

OpenAPI — spec, code generation, validation

Jab APIs ki sankhya badhi, toh unka shape aur structure consumers ke saath share karne ka tareeka chahiye tha. Isliye OpenAPI Initiative bani aur OpenAPI Specification (OAS) aayi. Swagger iska original reference implementation tha; aaj zyada tar tooling OpenAPI par converge ho gayi hai.

OpenAPI Specification kya hai

OAS ek JSON- ya YAML-based representation hai jo API ki structure, domain objects, aur security requirements ko describe karta hai. Isme metadata bhi hoti hai — legal/licensing, documentation, examples. Ye sirf documentation nahi hai; ye ek machine-readable contract hai jisse tools kaam kar sakte hain.

Code generation

OAS ka sabse useful feature: client-side code generate karna. OpenAPI Generator project kayi languages aur toolchains support karta hai — Java me Spring ya JAX-RS, TypeScript me tumhara favourite framework. Server-side ke stubs bhi generate kar sakte ho.

Lekin ek sawaal: pehle specification ya pehle code? OAS sirf API ka shape batata hai, semantics (expected behavior) nahi. Isliye sirf spec kaafi nahi hai — behavior ko model aur test bhi karna padta hai (Chapter 2 me contract testing dekhenge).

OpenAPI validation

OAS se request/response ko validate kar sakte ho — kya exchange specification se match karta hai? Ek practical use: DMZ (demilitarized zone) me messages ko check karna aur agar spec match na kare toh traffic ko terminate kar dena. Atlassian ne swagger-request-validator open source kiya hai jo JSON REST content validate karta hai.

// Specification se interaction validator banao
final OpenApiInteractionValidator validator =
  OpenApiInteractionValidator
    .createForSpecificationUrl(specUrl)
    .withBasePathOverride(basePathOverride)
    .build();
final ValidationReport report = validator.validate(request, response);
if (report.hasErrors()) {
  // Error information ko capture/process karo
}
SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 1
01.10Part I · Design, Build, Test

API versioning aur modeling exchanges

API versioning wo topic hai jo har API team ko pareshan karta hai. Naam badalna, field hatana, ya format badalna — sab compatibility tod sakta hai. Isliye versioning aur exchange modeling ko pehle se sochna padta hai.

Semantic Versioning (SemVer)

Version numbers ka ek standard tareeka hai: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Major version tab badhao jab breaking change ho, minor jab naya feature backward-compatible tareeke se add ho, patch jab bug fix ho. API versioning me ye discipline consumers ko batata hai ki kya expect karein.

Breaking changes se bacho

  • Naam mat badlo — field ya endpoint ka naam badalna breaking change hai.
  • Fields mat hatao — purane consumers unpar depend kar sakte hain.
  • Naye fields add karo — backward-compatible tareeke se (optional fields).
  • Pagination pehle se rakho — baad me array se object me badalna breaking hai (01.7 me dekha).

Modeling exchanges — format kaise chuno

  • High-traffic services: chhota, efficient format chahiye (jaise Protocol Buffers/gRPC).
  • Large payloads: streaming ya chunking socho; ek hi bada payload bhejna slow aur fragile hota hai.
  • HTTP/2 ke fayde: multiplexing, header compression, server push — high-traffic APIs ke liye HTTP/2 performance deta hai.
  • Vintage formats: purane formats (jaise XML/SOAP) ko support karna pad sakta hai legacy consumers ke liye, lekin naye APIs me JSON/Protobuf prefer karo.

Kya "golden specification" hai?

Ek hi specification jo sab kuch cover kare — aisa nahi hota. Multiple specifications (OpenAPI for REST, AsyncAPI for events, Protobuf for gRPC) ko combine karna padta hai. Challenge ye hai ki combined specifications ko consistent rakha jaaye. Koi ek perfect spec nahi hai; apne use case ke hisaab se chuno aur use consistently apply karo.

ADR Guideline: API standard chunte waqt socho — kya organization me pehle se koi standard hai? Kya third-party APIs (jaise Identity Services) ka koi standard hai jo tumhe expose karna hai? Standard na hone ka consumer par kya impact hoga? Standard ko organization ki culture aur existing APIs se match karo, aur use domain-specific amendments ke saath evolve karne ke liye taiyaar raho.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 1
02.1Part I · Design, Build, Test

Testing strategies — Test Quadrant (Q1–Q4)

Testing sirf ye ensure nahi karta ki application kaam karta hai — ye ensure karta hai ki wo sahi behavior dikhata hai. Lekin time aur resources limited hain, isliye har test likhna bekaar hai. Tumhe smartly decide karna hai ki kis type ke tests kitne hone chahiye. Iske liye do tools hain: Test Quadrant aur Test Pyramid.

Test Quadrant — Brian Marick, Agile Testing

Test quadrant technology aur business — dono perspectives ko jodta hai. Left side (Q1, Q2) product ko support karta hai (defects prevent karna); right side (Q3, Q4) product ko critique karta hai (defects dhoondhna). Upar (Q2, Q3) external quality hai (user ki expectations); neeche (Q1, Q4) internal quality hai (technology).

QuadrantKya test karta haiKaun
Q1Unit aur component tests — service sahi bana hai, pieces expected respond karte hainTechnology, automated
Q2Business ke saath tests — jo ban raha hai wo purpose serve karta haiBusiness + tech, automated + manual
Q3Business ke liye tests — functional requirements poori hain; exploratory testingBusiness, pehle manual, ab automated bhi
Q4Technical standpoint — production me cheez sahi chal rahi hai? (security, SLA, autoscaling)Technology, automated

Quadrant order nahi batata — ye guide karta hai ki kaunse tests chahiye. Kahan se shuru karna hai, ye tumhare factors par depend karta hai. Jaise ticketing system ko traffic spikes handle karne hain, toh pehle resilience (Q4, performance testing) se shuru karna behtar ho sakta hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 2
02.2Part I · Design, Build, Test

Test Pyramid — unit, service, end-to-end

Test Pyramid (Mike Cohn, Succeeding with Agile) batata hai ki har type ke test par kitna time lagana hai. Neeche unit tests (foundation, sabse zyada), beech me service tests, upar end-to-end tests (sabse kam, sabse slow).

Figure 2-3. The test pyramid, showing the proportion of tests desired

Pyramid ke teen hisse

  • Unit tests (neeche, sabse zyada): Code ke chhote, isolated units ko test karo. Agar test unit ki boundary se bahar jaaye, toh test doubles use karo (stubs — hardcoded responses; mocks — behavior verify karte hain). TDD (pehle test likho, phir logic) ka practice yahan fit hota hai. Ye Q1 me aate hain.
  • Service tests (beech me): Multiple units ek saath kaam kar rahe hain, behavior expected hai, application resilient hai — ye verify karo. Unit tests se zyada confidence, lekin zyada expensive (bada scope, kam isolation, zyada maintenance). Ye Q1, Q2, Q4 me aate hain.
  • End-to-end tests (upar, sabse kam): Poora request start se end tak flow karta hai. Sabse zyada confidence, lekin sabse bada scope, sabse slow, maintain karna sabse mushkil. Ye Q2, Q3, Q4 me aate hain.

Ice cream cone — galat shape

End-to-end testing par concentrate karna tempting hai kyunki wo zyada confidence deta hai. Lekin ye false sense of security hai — isse "ice cream cone" banta hai (pyramid ka ulta). End-to-end tests slow aur flaky hote hain; agar wo fail hon, toh pata nahi chalta ki problem kahan hai. Pyramid ko follow karo: zyada unit tests, kam E2E tests.

Trade-off yaad rakho: Chhote parts test karoge toh isolation aur speed achhi, lekin poora application kaam kar raha hai iska confidence kam. Poora application test karoge toh confidence zyada, lekin scope bada aur maintenance mushkil. Pyramid in dono ke beech balance hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 2
02.3Part I · Design, Build, Test

Contract testing — producer vs consumer-driven

Contract testing me do entities hain: consumer (API se data maangta hai) aur producer (API, data deta hai). Contract ek definition hai: agar consumer aisi request kare, toh producer aisa response dega. Ye dono ke beech ka agreement hai.

Contract kyun behtar hai

  • Breaking changes pakdo: Agar tum contract test todte ho, toh matlab producer contract fulfill nahi kar raha — consumers toot jayenge.
  • Stub server generate karo: Contract se stub server ban sakta hai jisse consumer develop aur test kar sakta hai bina producer ke.
  • Decoupling: Jab producer contract agree kar leta hai, toh consumer aur producer ek-doosre se independently build kar sakte hain. Dono deploy hone par seamlessly integrate ho jaate hain.
  • Local testing: Contract testing locally ho sakti hai — extra services launch karne ki zaroorat nahi.

Producer contracts vs Consumer-driven contracts (CDC)

Producer contractsConsumer-driven contracts (CDC)
Kaun define karta haiProducer khud apne contracts define karta haiConsumer batata hai use kya interaction chahiye; producer se discuss karke agree karte hain
Kab use karoJab API external third parties ke liye hai (jaise Microsoft Graph API — hazaaron consumers, koi ek consumer change nahi maang sakta)Jab consumer aur producer ek hi organization me hain aur aasani se baat kar sakte hain
FaydaShuru karna aasan hai; API ki integrity maintain rehti haiDiscussion se dono parties ko value milti hai — contract ek shared agreement banta hai

Note: Contract testing schema conformance jaisi nahi hai. Schema batata hai ki system compatible hai ya nahi; contract ek defined interaction hai jisme examples hote hain. Dono alag cheezein hain.

Contract.make {
  request {
    description('Get a list of all the attendees at a conference')
    method GET()
    url '/conference/1234/attendees'
    headers { contentType('application/json') }
  }
  response {
    status OK()
    headers { contentType('application/json') }
    body(
      value: [
        $(id: 123456, givenName: '[Name]', familyName: '[Name]'),
        $(id: 123457, givenName: '[Name]', familyName: '[Name]')
      ]
    )
  }
}

Is contract se tests aur stub server generate hote hain. Consumer stub se develop karta hai, producer tests se verify karta hai ki wo sahi interaction bana raha hai.

Galti mat karo: Contracts ko scenario tests ke liye use mat karo (jaise Step 1: attendee add karo, Step 2: list me check karo). Contracts interaction define karte hain; behavior test karna hai toh component tests use karo.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 2
02.4Part I · Design, Build, Test

Component testing vs integration testing

Contract testing ke baad, tumhe ye verify karna hai ki tumhara API sahi behavior dikhata hai (component testing) aur doosri services ke saath sahi integrate hota hai (integration testing). Dono alag hain.

Component testing — behavior verify karo

Component test me tum apne API ko ek request bhejte ho aur check karte ho ki response expected hai ya nahi. External dependencies ko mock kar dete ho (jaise DAO ko mock karna) taaki test sirf tumhare component par focus kare. Example: Attendee API ko ek request bhejo aur verify karo ki wo sahi attendee return karta hai.

Integration testing — doosri services ke saath

Integration testing me tum check karte ho ki tumhara API doosri services (jaise database, doosri APIs) ke saath sahi kaam karta hai. Isme real dependencies use hoti hain ya stub servers use hote hain.

Stub servers — kyun aur kaise

  • Kyun: Doosri service ko har baar run karna slow aur fragile hota hai. Stub server ek local service hai jo canned (pehle se tay) responses deta hai.
  • Kaise: Contract se stub generate karo, ya manually ek simple stub banao. Consumer stub ke against develop kar sakta hai bina real producer ke.
  • Recorder: Consumer stub server ke saath ek recorder use kar sakta hai jo real interactions ko capture karke stub me save karta hai.

Testcontainers — real dependencies, containers me

Testcontainers ek library hai jo tumhare tests ke liye real dependencies (jaise PostgreSQL, Kafka) ko Docker containers me run karti hai. Isse integration tests real environment ke kareeb hote hain, lekin phir bhi automated aur repeatable rehte hain. Case study me Testcontainers se verify kiya gaya ki Attendee API database ke saath sahi integrate hota hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 2
02.5Part I · Design, Build, Test

End-to-end testing — poora flow, automate karo

End-to-end (E2E) tests poora request flow check karte hain — start se end tak. Ye sabse zyada confidence dete hain, lekin sabse slow aur maintain karne me sabse mushkil bhi hote hain. Isliye inhe soch-samajh ke use karo.

E2E tests ke types

  • Happy path: Sab kuch sahi ho toh flow kaam karta hai (jaise attendee create karo, phir use list me dekho).
  • Error paths: Galat input ya failure par system sahi behave karta hai (jaise invalid attendee par 400 aata hai).
  • Cross-service: Request kayi services se hokar jaati hai aur ant me sahi result milta hai.

Automating E2E validation

E2E tests ko automate karna zaroori hai, warna wo manual aur slow ho jaate hain. Tooling ab itni advanced ho gayi hai ki Q3 (exploratory testing) ka bhi kaafi hissa automate ho sakta hai. Lekin yaad rakho: E2E tests ko pyramid ke upar kam rakhna hai — zyada E2E tests likhna ice cream cone banata hai.

ADR Guideline — testing strategy

Testing strategy chunte waqt socho: kya stakeholders ke paas time hai regularly discuss karne ka? Kya team ke paas skills hain in practices ko use karne ki? Kya workplace me koi internal strategy hai jo follow karni hai? Recommendation: test quadrant aur test pyramid dono use karo. Kam se kam test pyramid toh use karo hi — isse bugs development cycle me jaldi milte hain.

Summary (Ch 2): Test quadrant batata hai kaunse tests chahiye (business + technology), test pyramid batata hai kitne tests chahiye (zyada unit, kam E2E). Contract testing sabse zyada value deta hai (producer/consumer decoupling + stub generation). Component tests behavior verify karte hain, integration tests real dependencies check karte hain, E2E tests poora flow verify karte hain.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 2
03.1Part II · API Traffic Management

API Gateway kya hai — control plane aur data plane

API gateway ek management tool hai jo system ke edge par, consumer aur backend services ke beech me baithta hai. Ye ek defined group of APIs ke liye single point of entry hai. Consumer koi bhi ho sakta hai — mobile app, web app, internal system, ya third-party application.

Figure 3-1. Using an API gateway to route to the Attendee service

Do fundamental components

  • Control plane: Yahan operators interact karte hain — routes, policies, aur telemetry define karte hain. Ye "brain" hai.
  • Data plane: Yahan asal kaam hota hai — network packets route hote hain, policies enforce hoti hain, telemetry emit hoti hai. Ye "muscle" hai.

Dono ko ek saath package kar sakte ho ya alag-alag deploy kar sakte ho.

Gateway kya karta hai

Network level par API gateway ek reverse proxy ki tarah kaam karta hai: consumer ke saare API requests accept karo, unhe fulfill karne ke liye zaroori backend services ko call karo (aur aggregate karo), aur sahi result wapas do. Iske alawa ye cross-cutting requirements deta hai — user authentication, request rate limiting, timeouts/retries — aur observability ke liye metrics, logs, aur trace data deta hai.

Proxy, forward proxy, reverse proxy

  • Forward proxy: Clients ko protect karta hai. Business ka proxy employees ke traffic ko public internet par route aur filter karta hai.
  • Reverse proxy: Servers ko protect karta hai. Firewall ke peeche baith kar client requests ko sahi backend server par route karta hai. API gateway ek reverse proxy hai.
SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 3
03.2Part II · API Traffic Management

Proxy vs Load Balancer vs API Gateway

Proxy, load balancer, aur API gateway — teeno traffic ko route karte hain, lekin inka kaam alag hai. Galat tool chunna baad me pareshan karta hai. Isliye decision guideline samjho.

ToolKya karta haiKab use karo
Proxy (forward)Clients ke requests ko forward karta hai; clients ko protect karta haiJab tumhe outbound traffic ko control/filter karna hai
Reverse proxyBackend servers ke saamne baith kar requests ko route karta hai; servers ko protect karta haiJab ek simple entry point chahiye bina zyada features ke
Load balancerTraffic ko kayi backend instances me distribute karta hai (health checks ke saath)Jab traffic ko scale karna hai aur high availability chahiye
API gatewayReverse proxy + routing + auth + rate limiting + observability + lifecycle + developer portalJab tumhe APIs ko product ki tarah manage karna hai, kayi APIs aur consumers hain

Guideline — kaunsa chuno?

Socho: kya tumhe sirf traffic distribute karna hai (load balancer kaafi hai)? Kya tumhe ek simple entry point chahiye (reverse proxy kaafi hai)? Ya tumhe authentication, rate limiting, observability, API lifecycle management, aur developer onboarding chahiye (API gateway lo)?

Case study me: Attendee API ko mobile app se expose karna hai, PII hai (secure hona chahiye), reliable aur observable hona chahiye, aur aage aur APIs aane wali hain (alag languages/frameworks me). Sirf proxy/load balancer se kaam nahi chalega — API gateway sahi solution hai.

Yaad rakho: API gateway ko enterprise service bus (ESB) ki tarah use mat karo. Gateway ka kaam edge par traffic manage karna hai, business logic ya heavy transformation karna nahi. Agar gateway me business logic daal doge, toh wo ESB ban jaayega — aur wahi purani problems wapas aa jaayengi.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 3
03.3Part II · API Traffic Management

Gateway ki functionality — auth, rate limit, observability, lifecycle

API gateway sirf routing nahi karta — wo ek poora toolkit hai. Ye cross-cutting concerns ko ek jagah solve karta hai taaki har backend service ko alag se ye sab na karna pade.

Figure 3-6. An API gateway providing aggregation and translation

Key problems jo gateway solve karta hai

  • Coupling kam karo: Gateway ek facade/adapter ki tarah kaam karta hai. Clients gateway se integrate karte hain; backend change ho sakta hai (location, architecture, language) bina clients ko tode, jab tak contract same hai.
  • Consumption simplify karo: Aggregation/translation — ek client request ke liye kayi backend services ko call karo aur result ko ek response me jodo. Client ko kayi calls nahi karni padti.
  • Overuse/abuse se bachao: Threat detection aur mitigation — rate limiting, IP blocking, anomaly detection.
  • Observability: Metrics, logs, traces — kaunsi API kitni use ho rahi hai, kahan slow hai, kahan error hai.
  • API lifecycle management: API ko plan karo, design karo, deploy karo, deprecate karo, retire karo — poora lifecycle ek jagah se manage karo.
  • Monetization: Account management, billing, pay-per-use — API ko product ki tarah becho.

Aggregation aur translation

Ek client ko shayad ek screen ke liye 3 alag services se data chahiye. Bina gateway ke client ko 3 calls karni padti. Gateway ke saath client ek call karta hai, gateway 3 services ko call karta hai, results ko aggregate karta hai, aur ek response deta hai. Translation ka matlab hai: backend ka format (jaise gRPC/Protobuf) ko client ke format (jaise JSON/REST) me badalna.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 3
03.4Part II · API Traffic Management

Gateway kahan deploy karein — startup se enterprise tak

API gateway aam taur par system ke edge par deploy hota hai, lekin "system" ka matlab flexible hai. Startup me ek gateway kaafi hota hai; enterprise me kayi gateways alag-alag jagah hote hain.

Figure 3-1. Using an API gateway to route to the Attendee service

Startup / SMB deployment

Ek hi API gateway (high availability ke liye multiple instances) jo poore backend estate ka front door hai. Ye saari edge functionality deta hai — routing, auth, rate limiting, observability. Simple aur kaafi hai.

Enterprise deployment

Kayi gateways alag-alag jagah: data center ke perimeter par ek edge stack, aur har product/line of business/department ke liye alag gateway. Har gateway ki functionality alag ho sakti hai — geographical location (governance requirements) ya infrastructure capabilities (low-powered edge compute) ke hisaab se. Gateway aksar public internet aur DMZ (demilitarized zone) ke beech me baithta hai.

Edge stack — kayi layers

Modern edge stack me kayi layers hote hain: load balancer, API gateway, WAF (web application firewall), CDN, authentication. Ye layers ek monolithic component nahi hain — ye alag-alag deploy hote hain aur alag teams ya third-party providers operate karte hain. Kuch API gateways poora edge stack dete hain; kuch sirf gateway functionality dete hain; cloud vendors load balancer dete hain jo gateway se integrate hota hai.

Single point of failure?

Jab saara user traffic ek edge gateway se jaata hai, toh wo single point of failure ban sakta hai. Isliye gateway ko highly available deploy karo (multiple instances, multiple zones), aur socho ki agar gateway down ho jaaye toh kya hoga. Gateway ka failure poora system down kar sakta hai — isliye iski reliability par dhyan do.

Summary (Ch 3): API gateway edge par single entry point hai (control plane + data plane). Ye reverse proxy se zyada hai — auth, rate limiting, observability, lifecycle, monetization deta hai. Proxy/load balancer se alag hai — unhe sirf routing/distribution ke liye use karo, gateway ko API product management ke liye. Gateway ko ESB mat banao.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 3
04.1Part II · API Traffic Management

Service mesh kya hai — sidecar, data plane, control plane

Chapter 3 me tumne ingress traffic (north–south, bahar se andar) manage karna seekha. Ab internal APIs ka traffic (east–west, service-to-service) manage karna seekho. Iske liye service mesh hai — routing, observing, aur securing traffic for service-to-service communication.

Figure 4-1. C4 Model showing the extraction of the Session service

Service mesh kaise kaam karta hai

Service mesh me har service ke saath ek sidecar proxy deploy hota hai (jaise Envoy). Tumhara application code seedha doosri service ko call nahi karta — wo sidecar ko call karta hai, aur sidecar request ko route karta hai, security enforce karta hai, aur telemetry emit karta hai. Application code ko ye sab pata bhi nahi chalta.

  • Data plane: Sidecar proxies — ye asal traffic handle karte hain (routing, retries, timeouts, mTLS, metrics).
  • Control plane: Ye sidecars ko configure karta hai — routing rules, security policies, observability settings. Tum control plane se poora mesh manage karte ho.

Case study — Session service nikaalna

Ab conference system se sessions-handling functionality ko nikaal kar ek naya internally facing Session service banaya jaata hai. Ab Session service ko Attendee service aur legacy monolith se baat karni hai. Tum API gateway use kar sakte ho, lekin ye suboptimal hoga — gateway ingress (north–south) ke liye hai, internal service-to-service (east–west) ke liye service mesh behtar hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 4
04.2Part II · API Traffic Management

Service mesh vs libraries — kab kya chuno

Service-to-service communication ke liye do approaches hain: language-specific libraries (SDK/database driver) ya service mesh. Dono kaam kar sakte hain — decision tumhare requirements par depend karta hai.

Libraries kab kaafi hain

  • Single programming language hai organization me.
  • Simple routing chahiye (REST/RPC calls, zyada features nahi).
  • Cross-functional requirements (auth, rate limiting) simple hain ya nahi chahiye.

Service mesh kab chuno

  • Kayi languages hain — har language me library maintain karna mushkil hai; mesh language-agnostic hai.
  • Advanced features chahiye — authentication, authorization, rate limiting, observability, traffic management.
  • Consumers/providers ki sankhya badh rahi hai — mesh scalable, maintainable, aur secure option hai.
  • Organization-wide mandate hai ki saara traffic mesh se jaaye.

ADR Guideline: "Kya hume service mesh use karna chahiye ya library?" — Socho: kya ek hi language hai? Kya sirf simple routing chahiye? Kya advanced cross-functional features chahiye? Kya pehle se koi solution hai? In sawalon ke jawab se decide karo. Mesh free lunch nahi hai — iski complexity aur operational cost bhi hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 4
04.3Part II · API Traffic Management

Mesh kya deta hai — routing, observability, security

Service mesh teen cheezein deta hai: fine-grained routing, transparent observability, aur security enforcement. Aur ye sab application code change kiye bina — sidecar ke through.

Figure 4-3. A typical service mesh topology, deployed across two clusters

Fine-grained control of routing, reliability, traffic management

Traffic ko version ke hisaab se split karo (canary), retries aur timeouts set karo, circuit breaking lagao (agar ek service fail ho rahi hai, toh use aur requests mat bhejo). Ye sab mesh ke control plane se configure hota hai, code change kiye bina.

Transparent observability

Har sidecar metrics, logs, aur traces emit karta hai. Tumhe har service me observability code likhne ki zaroorat nahi — mesh automatically batata hai ki request kahan se kahan gayi, kitna time laga, kahan error aaya.

Security — transport security, authentication, authorization

Mesh mTLS (mutual TLS) enforce karta hai — har service ek-doosre ko verify karti hai. Authentication aur authorization bhi mesh level par enforce hoti hai. Isse tumhe har service me security code nahi likhna padta.

Cross-functional communication across languages

Ek service Java me hai, doosri Go me, teesri Python me — mesh in sab ke beech communication ko uniform tareeke se handle karta hai. Har service ko apni language ki library ki zaroorat nahi.

Ingress aur service-to-service ko alag rakho

API gateway ingress (north–south) ke liye hai; service mesh service-to-service (east–west) ke liye hai. Dono ko alag rakho — gateway ko mesh ki jagah use mat karo aur mesh ko gateway ki jagah use mat karo.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 4
04.4Part II · API Traffic Management

Mesh taxonomy aur evolution — sidecar, proxyless, eBPF

Service mesh ek hi tarah ka nahi hota. Iske implementation patterns alag hain, aur technology evolve ho rahi hai. Ye samajhna zaroori hai taaki tum sahi pattern chuno.

Figure 4-6. Service mesh proxies forming a higher-level networking abstraction

Implementation patterns

  • Sidecar: Har service instance ke saath ek proxy container chalta hai. Ye sabse common pattern hai (Istio, Linkerd). Iska fayda: har service ko apna proxy milta hai, isolation achhi hai. Nuksaan: resource overhead (har instance ke saath ek aur container).
  • Proxyless (gRPC): Kuch frameworks (jaise gRPC) mesh functionality ko library me hi implement karte hain — alag sidecar nahi chahiye. Ye lightweight hai lekin sirf un frameworks tak limited hai.
  • Node-level proxy (Cilium/eBPF): Ek node par ek Envoy proxy chalta hai jo saari services ko serve karta hai. eBPF kernel level par networking ko handle karta hai. Isse resource overhead kam hota hai.

Evolution of service mesh

Service mesh shuru me simple tha — sirf routing aur observability. Phir security (mTLS), traffic management (canary, circuit breaking), aur policy enforcement add hui. Ab mesh multi-cluster aur multi-cloud tak pahunch gaya hai. Technology abhi bhi evolve ho rahi hai — isliye apne use case ke hisaab se chuno, hype ke hisaab se nahi.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 4
04.5Part II · API Traffic Management

Case study — Istio routing, Linkerd observability, Consul segmentation

Book me service mesh ko teen tools se demonstrate kiya gaya hai — har ek apni strength ke liye. Ye case study batata hai ki mesh ko real me kaise use karte hain.

Routing with Istio

Istio se traffic routing configure kiya gaya — kaunsi version ko kitna traffic jaaye, retries aur timeouts kya hon. Istio ka control plane (Istiod) saare sidecars ko configure karta hai. Tum YAML me routing rules likhte ho aur Istio use enforce karta hai.

Observing traffic with Linkerd

Linkerd se traffic ko observe kiya gaya — linkerd viz se services ke beech traffic flow dekha ja sakta hai, aur Grafana dashboards se metrics dekh sakte ho. Linkerd lightweight hai aur observability par focus karta hai.

Network segmentation with Consul

Consul se network segmentation kiya gaya — kaunsi service kis se baat kar sakti hai, ye policy se define karo. Isse security badhti hai: agar ek service compromise ho jaaye, toh wo har jagah nahi pahunch sakti.

Deploying a service mesh — failure ko samjho

  • Single point of failure: Agar control plane down ho jaaye, toh sidecars purani config par chalte rehte hain (data plane independent hai). Lekin nayi config deploy nahi ho sakti. Isliye control plane ko highly available rakho.
  • Too many networking layers: Gateway + mesh + load balancer + service discovery — bahut saare layers ho sakte hain. Har layer ki zaroorat samjho; bina matlab ke layers mat add karo.
  • Service mesh as ESB: Mesh ko ESB (enterprise service bus) ki tarah use mat karo — mesh ka kaam networking hai, business logic ya heavy transformation nahi.
  • Service mesh as gateway: Mesh ko ingress gateway ki tarah use mat karo — ingress ke liye API gateway hai.

Checklist — mesh select karte waqt: Requirements identify karo (kya chahiye — routing? security? observability?). Build vs buy decide karo (khud banao ya managed service lo?). Har option ko requirements ke against evaluate karo. Koi perfect mesh nahi hai — apne use case ke liye best chuno.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 4
05.1Part III · Operations & Security

Deployment vs release — feature flags

Deployment aur release — dono alag cheezein hain, aur inhe alag rakhna hi sahi tareeka hai. Deployment ka matlab hai code ko production me daalna; release ka matlab hai users ko feature dikhana. Dono ko alag karne se tum code deploy kar sakte ho bina use release kiye, aur release kar sakte ho bina dobara deploy kiye.

Feature flags — deployment aur release ko alag karne ka tareeka

Feature flags (feature toggles) ek configuration hai jo code ko deploy karne ke baad bhi feature ko on/off kar sakti hai. Feature flag typically ek configuration store me hota hai (application ke bahar), aur code deploy hota hai feature off ke saath. Jab team ready ho, toh flag ko on kar do — application alag branch execute karta hai.

// LaunchDarkly example (pseudocode)
LDUser user = new LDUser("[Name]@example.com");
boolean newAttendeesService =
  launchDarklyClient.boolVariation("user.enabled.modern", user, false);
if (newAttendeesService) {
  // modern store se attendee lao
} else {
  // legacy store se attendee lao
}

Isse tum chhote batch of users ko naye system par migrate kar sakte ho aur test kar sakte ho. Agar kuch galat ho, toh flag ko wapas off kar do — rollback aasan hai. Rollout 100% tak badha sakte ho dheere-dheere.

Knight Capital — $460 million ka lesson: Feature flags ko saaf karna zaroori hai. Ek baar migration complete ho jaaye, toh feature flag code ko poori tarah hata do. Knight Capital ne ek feature flag reuse kiya aur ek failed deployment ke saath, hazaaron dollars per second ka nuksaan hua — ant me $460 million ka loss. Feature flags ko unique naam do aur kaam khatam hone par hata do.

Graceful degradation: Agar feature-flagging service fail ho jaaye, toh wo catastrophic ho sakta hai (single point of failure). Isliye last known value ko cache me rakho ya default values do taaki application chalta rahe.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 5
05.2Part III · Operations & Security

Traffic management aur K8s deployment

API-based architecture ka fayda hai ki tum jaldi iterate kar sakte ho aur Attendee service me naye changes deploy kar sakte ho. Traffic ko do jagah manipulate kar sakte ho: API gateway ingress par ya service mesh ke andar.

Kubernetes me deployment ka flow

  1. Pull request banao; approve aur merge hone par deployment build automatically start hoti hai.
  2. Build pipeline Docker/OCI image banati hai.
  3. Image ko container registry me push karo.
  4. Deployment ko target environment me trigger karo.

By default Kubernetes running deployment ko naye deployment se replace kar deta hai. Lekin release strategies (canary, blue-green, mirroring) se tum release ko phase kar sakte ho — deployment complete hone ke baad, release configuration alag se follow hoti hai.

API Lifecycle

API ka ek lifecycle hota hai: planning → design → develop → test → deploy → operate → deprecate → retire. Har stage par alag decisions hote hain. Release strategies ko lifecycle se map karna zaroori hai — jaise ek nayi API ko pehle beta me release karo, phir GA (general availability) me, phir purani version ko deprecate karo.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 5
05.3Part III · Operations & Security

Release strategies — canary, mirroring, blue-green

Release strategies batati hain ki naya version users tak kaise pahunchaya jaaye. Har strategy ka apna risk aur fayda hai. Tumhe apne use case ke hisaab se chunna hai.

Figure 5-2. Deploying the Attendee service using a canary approach
StrategyKaise kaam karta haiFaydaRisk
CanaryNaye version ko chhote % users ko do (jaise 5%), phir dheere-dheere badhao (20% → 50% → 100%)Problem jaldi pakdo, kam users affect hote hainMonitoring zaroori hai; agar metrics nahi dekhe toh problem miss ho sakti hai
Traffic mirroringReal traffic ko naye version par bhi bhejo (copy), lekin response sirf purane version se loNaya version real traffic se test hota hai bina users ko affect kiyeNaya version ko double traffic handle karna padta hai; side effects (jaise writes) se bacho
Blue-greenDo environments rakho (blue = current, green = new). Green ko test karo, phir traffic ko ek saath green par switch karoRollback instant hai (wapas blue par switch karo); downtime nahiDouble infrastructure chahiye; database migration tricky ho sakta hai

Argo Rollouts — case study

Book me Argo Rollouts se rollouts perform kiye gaye hain. Argo Rollouts ek Kubernetes controller hai jo canary aur blue-green strategies ko automate karta hai. Tum rollout YAML me steps define karte ho (jaise 20% weight, phir pause, phir 50%), aur Argo Rollouts use execute karta hai. Agar metrics kharab hon, toh rollout automatically rollback ho sakta hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 5
05.4Part III · Operations & Security

Blue-green aur Argo Rollouts — deep dive

Blue-green ek simple aur powerful strategy hai. Tum do identical environments rakhte ho aur traffic ko ek se doosre par switch karte ho. Argo Rollouts is process ko automate karta hai.

Figure 5-4. Deploying the Attendee service using a blue-green approach

Blue-green kaise kaam karta hai

  • Blue — current live version (users yahi use kar rahe hain).
  • Green — naya version (deploy ho gaya hai, lekin traffic nahi aa raha).
  • Green ko test karo (smoke tests, manual checks). Agar sab theek hai, toh traffic ko green par switch karo (ek saath).
  • Agar problem aaye, toh wapas blue par switch karo — rollback instant hai.

Argo Rollouts steps

Argo Rollouts me tum steps define karte ho: pehle 20% weight par release karo, phir pause karo (manual approval ya automated analysis), phir 50%, phir 100%. Har step par metrics check hote hain — agar error rate badhe ya latency badhe, toh rollout ruk jaata hai ya rollback hota hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 5
05.5Part III · Operations & Security

Observability — three pillars, metrics, signals

Release karne ke baad tumhe pata hona chahiye ki wo kaam kar raha hai ya nahi. Iske liye observability chahiye — system ke andar kya ho raha hai, ye dekhne ki ability. Observability ke three pillars hain: metrics, logs, aur traces.

Three pillars of observability

  • Metrics: Numbers jo time ke saath change hote hain (jaise request count, error rate, latency). Metrics se tum trends dekh sakte ho aur alerts set kar sakte ho.
  • Logs: Events ka record (jaise "user X ne attendee Y create kiya"). Logs se tum specific incidents ko debug kar sakte ho.
  • Traces: Ek request ka poora journey — kaunsi service se kaunsi service gayi, har jagah kitna time laga. Distributed tracing (jaise Jaeger, Zipkin) se tum bottlenecks dhoondh sakte ho.

APIs ke liye important metrics

  • Request rate: Kitne requests per second aa rahe hain?
  • Error rate: Kitne % requests fail ho rahe hain (4xx/5xx)?
  • Latency: Request ko respond karne me kitna time lagta hai (p50, p95, p99)?
  • Saturation: System kitna busy hai (CPU, memory, queue depth)?

Signals padhna — kya dekhna hai

Metrics ko dekh kar "signals" padho: agar error rate achanak badhe, toh kuch toota hai. Agar latency badhe, toh koi service slow hai ya database me problem hai. Agar request rate badhe, toh traffic spike hai — autoscaling chahiye. Signals ko samajhna ek skill hai — practice se aati hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 5
05.6Part III · Operations & Security

Caching, logging, opinionated platform

Release ke baad bhi kuch application-level decisions hote hain jo releases ko effective banate hain: response caching, header propagation, logging, aur ek opinionated platform ka use.

Response caching

Har request par backend ko hit karna zaroori nahi hai. Agar response change nahi hota (jaise attendee list), toh use cache karo — API gateway ya CDN par. Isse latency kam hoti hai aur backend par load kam padta hai. Lekin cache invalidation sochna padta hai — jab data change ho, toh cache ko update karo.

Application-level header propagation

Request ke saath headers (jaise correlation ID, user context) ko saari services me propagate karo. Isse tracing aur debugging aasan hoti hai — ek request ko end-to-end track kar sakte ho.

Logging to assist debugging

Logs structured hone chahiye (JSON format) taaki unhe search aur analyze kar sakein. Har log me correlation ID, timestamp, service name, aur relevant context hona chahiye. Logs ko centralize karo (jaise ELK stack) taaki saari services ke logs ek jagah dekhe ja sakein.

Opinionated platform

Ek opinionated platform wo hai jo teams ko ek standard tareeka deta hai APIs banane aur deploy karne ka — templates, golden paths, aur best practices. Isse har team ko dobara decide nahi karna padta ki kaise deploy karein, kaise monitor karein. Platform team ye sab provide karti hai aur product teams us par build karti hain.

ADR Guideline: "Kya hume opinionated platform banana chahiye?" — Socho: kya teams ko standard chahiye? Kya platform team ke paas bandwidth hai? Kya teams platform ko adopt karenge? Opinionated platform tab kaam karta hai jab wo teams ki madad karta hai, unhe restrict nahi karta.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 5
06.1Part III · Operations & Security

Threat modeling 101 — OWASP aur Attendee API

APIs ko secure karna optional nahi hai — ye zaroori hai. External APIs ko secure na karne ka risk bahut bada hai: data breach, unauthorized access, service disruption. Threat modeling wo process hai jisse tum pehle se soch lete ho ki tumhare system par kya attacks ho sakte hain aur unse kaise bacha jaaye.

Figure 6-1. The Attendee API that will be used in the threat modeling exercise

Case study — OWASP ko Attendee API par apply karna

Book me Attendee API par OWASP (Open Web Application Security Project) API Security Top 10 apply kiya gaya hai. OWASP API Top 10 me common API vulnerabilities hain — jaise broken object level authorization, broken authentication, excessive data exposure, lack of resources/rate limiting, broken function level authorization, mass assignment, security misconfiguration, injection, improper assets management, insufficient logging/monitoring.

External APIs ko secure na karne ka risk

  • Data breach: PII (jaise attendee emails) leak ho sakta hai.
  • Unauthorized access: Koi bhi kisi ka data dekh ya badal sakta hai.
  • Service disruption: Attacker API ko overload karke down kar sakta hai.
  • Reputation aur legal: Data breach se company ki reputation kharab hoti hai aur legal consequences ho sakte hain (GDPR, etc.).
SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 6
06.2Part III · Operations & Security

Threat modeling ke 6 steps

Threat modeling ek structured process hai. Book me 6 steps diye gaye hain. Inhe follow karke tum systematically apne system ke threats identify kar sakte ho.

Step 1: Identify your objectives

Tum kya protect karna chahte ho? Attendee API ke liye objective hai: attendees ki PII ko protect karna, unauthorized access rokna, aur service ko available rakhna.

Step 2: Gather the right information

System ke baare me information ikattha karo — architecture diagrams, data flows, APIs, dependencies. Bina system ko samjhe threats nahi dhoondh sakte.

Step 3: Decompose the system

System ko chhote parts me todo — data flow diagram banao. Kahan se data aata hai, kahan jaata hai, kahan store hota hai, kahan process hota hai. Har boundary (trust boundary) ko mark karo — jahan data ek trust zone se doosre me jaata hai, wahan threat ho sakta hai.

Step 4: Identify threats — STRIDE

STRIDE methodology se threats identify karo (agle section me detail me).

Step 5: Evaluate threat risks

Har threat ka risk evaluate karo — kitna likely hai aur kitna impact hoga? High likelihood + high impact = pehle fix karo. Low likelihood + low impact = baad me ya accept karo.

Step 6: Validation

Mitigations ko validate karo — kya tumne jo fix lagaya wo kaam karta hai? Penetration testing, code review, aur automated scanning se validate karo.

Thinking like an attacker: Threat modeling karte waqt attacker ki tarah socho. Attacker kya chahta hai? Wo kaise andar aayega? Wo kya nuksaan pahuncha sakta hai? Ye mindset threats dhoondhne me madad karta hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 6
06.3Part III · Operations & Security

STRIDE — 6 threat categories

STRIDE ek methodology hai jo Praerit Garg aur Loren Kohnfelder ne design ki thi. Ye 6 threat categories ka acronym hai. Har category ek type ke attack ko represent karti hai.

LetterThreatMatlabExample (Attendee API)
SSpoofingKoi aur ban kar aana — authentication ko bypass karnaAttacker kisi aur attendee ki identity use karke uska data dekhta hai
TTamperingData ko bina pata chale badal denaAttacker request me attendee ki details badal deta hai (jaise email change kar deta hai)
RRepudiationYe kehna ki "maine ye nahi kiya" — bina proof ke deny karnaEk user attendee delete karta hai aur kehta hai "maine nahi kiya"; logs nahi hain toh prove nahi kar sakte
IInformation DisclosureSensitive information leak honaAPI error message me stack trace ya doosre attendees ki details leak ho jaati hain
DDenial of ServiceService ko unusable bana denaAttacker bahut saare requests bhej kar API ko overload kar deta hai
EElevation of PrivilegeZyada permissions paa lena jo tumhe nahi milni chahiyeEk normal user admin ka kaam kar leta hai (jaise saare attendees delete kar deta hai)

Data flow diagram par STRIDE apply karte ho: har element (process, data store, data flow, external entity) par socho ki kaunsa STRIDE threat lag sakta hai. Phir har threat ke liye mitigation socho.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 6
06.4Part III · Operations & Security

Mitigations — rate limiting, load shedding, validation

Threats identify karne ke baad unhe mitigate karna hai. Book me kuch key mitigations diye gaye hain jo API gateway par implement kiye ja sakte hain.

Figure 6-4. Rate limiting example with the API gateway

Rate limiting

Rate limiting ka matlab hai: ek consumer ek time me kitne requests bhej sakta hai, use limit karo. Jaise 100 requests per minute per API key. Isse DoS attacks aur accidental overuse se bachte hain. API gateway par rate limiting lagana aasan hai — har consumer ki limit define karo aur exceed hone par 429 Too Many Requests return karo.

Load shedding

Load shedding ka matlab hai: jab system overload ho, toh kuch requests ko jaan-bujh kar drop kar do taaki system poori tarah down na ho. Isse critical requests ko serve kar sakte ho aur system ko recover karne ka time milta hai. Ye circuit breaking jaisa hai — jab system struggle kar raha ho, toh load kam karo.

Input validation

Har request ko validate karo — kya data expected format me hai? Kya required fields hain? Kya values valid range me hain? OpenAPI validation (Ch 1 me dekha) se request/response ko spec ke against validate kar sakte ho. Invalid requests ko early reject karo — backend tak mat jaane do.

Threat modeling ka summary

Threat modeling ek baar ka kaam nahi hai — ye continuous process hai. Jab system change ho, toh dobara threat model karo. STRIDE se threats identify karo, risk evaluate karo, mitigations lagao, aur validate karo. Yehi secure API architecture ki neev hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 6
07.1Part III · Operations & Security

Authentication — tokens, keys, users

Authentication ka matlab hai: tum kaun ho? Authorization ka matlab hai: tum kya kar sakte ho? Dono alag hain aur dono zaroori hain. Is chapter me authentication aur authorization ko detail me samjhenge.

End-user authentication with tokens

End users (jaise mobile app users) tokens se authenticate karte hain. User login karta hai, server ek token deta hai (jaise JWT), aur user har request me wo token bhejta hai. Server token ko verify karke user ko pehchanta hai.

System-to-system authentication

Jab ek system doosre system se baat karta hai (jaise CFP system Attendee API ko call karta hai), toh user nahi hota — system hota hai. Iske liye API keys ya client credentials use hote hain. API key ek secret hota hai jo system apni identity prove karne ke liye bhejta hai.

Keys aur users ko mix mat karo

API keys users ke liye nahi hain aur user tokens systems ke liye nahi hain. Dono ko mix karna security problem hai:

  • API keys: Long-lived hote hain, revoke karna mushkil hota hai, aur inme user context nahi hota. Ye system-to-system ke liye hain.
  • User tokens: Short-lived hote hain, user ki identity aur permissions carry karte hain. Ye end-user ke liye hain.

Agar tum API key ko user ki tarah use karoge, toh tumhe pata nahi chalega ki kaunsa user request kar raha hai, aur key leak hone par use revoke karna mushkil hoga.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 7
07.2Part III · Operations & Security

OAuth2 aur JWT — roles, tokens, grants

OAuth2 ek authorization framework hai jo third-party applications ko limited access deta hai bina user ka password share kiye. Ye aaj ka standard hai API authorization ke liye.

OAuth2 roles

  • Resource Owner: User jiska data hai (jaise attendee).
  • Client: Application jo data access karna chahti hai (jaise mobile app).
  • Authorization Server: Jo tokens issue karta hai (jaise login server).
  • Resource Server: Jo API host karta hai (jaise Attendee API). Ye tokens ko verify karta hai.

JSON Web Tokens (JWT)

JWT (pronounced "jot") ek token format hai jo claims (key-value pairs) carry karta hai. JWT ke teen parts hote hain: header, payload, signature — jo dot (.) se alag hote hain. JWT ko do tareeke se secure kiya jaata hai:

  • JWS (JSON Web Signatures): JWT ko sign karta hai taaki integrity bani rahe — koi token ko badal na sake. Jab log "JWT" kehte hain, toh aam taur par unka matlab JWS-signed JWT hota hai.
  • JWE (JSON Web Encryption): JWT ko encrypt karta hai taaki contents confidential rahein. Encrypted JWT ka matlab hai JWE use ho raha hai.

JWT me confidential data mat daalo: Agar JWT JWS use kar raha hai (sirf signed, encrypt nahi), toh uska payload koi bhi padh sakta hai (base64 decode karke). Isliye JWT me passwords ya sensitive data mat rakho. Confidential data ke liye JWE (encryption) use karo.

Reserved claims

JWT RFC me kuch reserved claims hain jinka special meaning hai: iss (issuer), sub (subject — kis user ke liye hai), exp (expiry), iat (issued at), jti (JWT ID — unique identifier). Inhe sahi tareeke se use karo.

eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.
eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ.
SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c

Ye ek example JWT hai — header, payload, signature (dot se alag).

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 7
07.3Part III · Operations & Security

OAuth2 grants — Auth Code, PKCE, Client Credentials

OAuth2 me alag-alag "grants" hain — har grant ek tareeka hai token paane ka. Kaunsa grant use karna hai, ye tumhare scenario par depend karta hai.

Figure 7-6. Authorization Code Grant

Authorization Code Grant

Ye sabse common aur secure grant hai web/mobile apps ke liye. Flow: user authorization server par login karta hai → authorization code milta hai → client code ko token se exchange karta hai. Token client ko directly nahi milta, pehle code milta hai — isse token leak hone ka risk kam hota hai.

Authorization Code Grant + PKCE

PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange, pronounced "pixie") Authorization Code Grant ka extension hai jo mobile/native apps ke liye hai. Isme client ek code verifier aur code challenge banata hai. Jab code ko token se exchange karte ho, toh verifier bhi bhejte ho — isse pata chalta hai ki wahi client hai jisne code maanga tha. Public clients (mobile apps) ke liye PKCE use karna chahiye.

Refresh Tokens

Access tokens short-lived hote hain (jaise 1 hour). Jab wo expire ho jaaye, toh refresh token se naya access token le sakte ho bina user ko dobara login karaye. Refresh tokens long-lived hote hain aur securely store karne chahiye.

Client Credentials Grant

Jab ek system doosre system se baat karta hai (koi user nahi hai), toh Client Credentials Grant use hota hai. Client apni client ID aur secret se directly token leta hai. Ye system-to-system authentication ke liye hai.

Additional grants

OAuth2 me aur bhi grants hain (jaise Device Code Grant for TV/IoT devices, Resource Owner Password Credentials — lekin ye deprecated hai kyunki user ko apna password client ko dena padta hai). Aaj ke time me Authorization Code + PKCE aur Client Credentials sabse zyada use hote hain.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 7
07.4Part III · Operations & Security

Scopes, enforcement, OIDC, SAML

OAuth2 me scopes batate hain ki token ko kya-kya karne ki permission hai. Scope ke bina token ka matlab nahi hai — token ko hamesha ek scope ke saath issue karna chahiye.

Figure 7-7. Authorization Code Grant + PKCE

OAuth2 Scopes

Scope ek string hoti hai jo permission describe karti hai — jaise read:attendees (attendees ko padh sakte ho) ya write:attendees (attendees ko badal sakte ho). Client sirf wahi scopes maang sakta hai jo use chahiye (least privilege). Authorization server user se poochta hai ki kya wo in scopes ko allow karta hai.

Authorization enforcement

Token milne ke baad use enforce karna hai — resource server (API gateway ya API khud) token ko verify karta hai aur check karta hai ki usme required scope hai ya nahi. Agar scope nahi hai, toh 403 Forbidden return karo. Enforcement API gateway par bhi ho sakta hai aur service level par bhi.

OIDC (OpenID Connect)

OIDC OAuth2 ke upar ek identity layer hai. OAuth2 authorization ke liye hai (kya kar sakte ho); OIDC authentication ke liye hai (tum kaun ho). OIDC se tumhe ek id_token milta hai jo user ki identity batata hai. Aaj ke time me OIDC standard hai user login ke liye.

SAML 2.0

SAML ek purana standard hai (XML-based) jo enterprise SSO (single sign-on) ke liye use hota hai. OIDC aaj zyada popular hai kyunki wo JSON-based aur mobile-friendly hai, lekin SAML abhi bhi kai enterprises me use hota hai. Dono ka kaam same hai — user ki identity verify karna — lekin OIDC modern hai.

ADR Guideline — OAuth2 grants chunte waqt: Kaunsa grant use karna hai? Socho: kya user involved hai (Auth Code + PKCE)? Kya system-to-system hai (Client Credentials)? Kya token ko refresh karna hai (Refresh Tokens)? Har scenario ke liye sahi grant chuno — galat grant security hole ban sakta hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 7
08.1Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

APIs se system evolve kyun karein

Systems change hote hain — nayi requirements aati hain, technology badalti hai, business evolve karta hai. APIs tumhe system ko evolve karne ka tareeka deti hain bina poora system dobara likhe. Ye chapter batata hai ki APIs ko evolution ka tool kaise banaya jaaye.

Figure 8-1. Proposal for module breakdown in the conference case study

Useful abstractions — cohesion badhao

Ek achhi abstraction wo hai jo ek cheez ko achhi tarah represent kare aur baaki details ko chhupaye. APIs abstractions banati hain — har API ek clear purpose serve karta hai. Jab abstractions achhi hoti hain, toh system ko samajhna aur change karna aasan hota hai.

Domain boundaries — loose coupling

Domain boundaries batati hain ki kahan ek domain khatam hota hai aur doosra shuru hota hai. Attendee domain ki boundary clear hai — wo attendees ko manage karta hai, sessions ko nahi. Jab boundaries clear hote hain, toh services loosely coupled hoti hain — ek service change karne se doosri nahi tootti.

Case study — Attendee domain boundaries

Conference system me Attendee domain ki boundaries establish ki gayi: Attendee service attendees ko manage karta hai, Session service sessions ko, aur dono ke beech ek clear API contract hai. Isse dono services independently evolve kar sakti hain.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 8
08.2Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

End-state options — monolith, SOA, microservices, functions

Jab tum system ko evolve karte ho, toh tumhe ek end-state architecture chunna hota hai. Har option ke apne trade-offs hain — koi ek perfect nahi hai.

OptionKya haiKab chuno
MonolithEk hi deployable unit — saara code ek jagahJab team chhoti hai, domain simple hai, aur deployment simple rakhna hai
SOA (Service-Oriented Architecture)Services jo business capabilities ko represent karte hain, ESB se connect hote hainEnterprise me jahan services ko share karna hai (lekin ESB ke nuksaan se bacho)
MicroservicesChhote, independent services jo apna data aur deployment rakhte hainJab team badi hai, services ko independently deploy/scale karna hai
Functions (Serverless)Event-driven functions jo on-demand chalte hainJab workload bursty hai aur tum infrastructure manage nahi karna chahte

Yaad rakho: End-state ek destination nahi hai — ye ek direction hai. Tum monolith se shuru karke dheere-dheere microservices ki taraf ja sakte ho, ya monolith me hi reh sakte ho agar wo kaam karta hai. Architecture ko business needs ke hisaab se evolve karo, hype ke hisaab se nahi.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 8
08.3Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

Evolutionary process — goals, fitness functions, decomposing

System ko evolve karna ek process hai, ek event nahi. Is process me goals set karna, fitness functions use karna, aur system ko modules me todna shamil hai.

Determine your goals

Pehle decide karo ki tum kya achieve karna chahte ho. Kya tum scalability chahte ho? Kya tum deployment speed chahte ho? Kya tum team autonomy chahte ho? Goals clear hone se decisions aasan hote hain.

Using fitness functions

Fitness functions automated checks hain jo batate hain ki tumhara architecture tumhare goals ko meet kar raha hai ya nahi. Jaise: "koi service doosri service ke database ko directly access nahi kar sakti" — ye ek fitness function hai jo architectural rule ko enforce karta hai. Fitness functions ko CI/CD me run karo taaki violations jaldi pakde jaayein.

Decomposing a system into modules

Monolith ko modules me todo — har module ek clear responsibility rakhta hai. Phir modules ke beech APIs banao ("seams"). Ye APIs woh jagah hain jahan tum system ko tod sakte ho aur alag services me badal sakte ho.

APIs as "seams" for extension

Ek "seam" wo jagah hai jahan tum system me naya behavior add kar sakte ho bina purane code ko badle. APIs seams banati hain — tum nayi functionality ko API ke peeche add kar sakte ho aur purana code untouched rehta hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 8
08.4Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

Patterns — Strangler Fig, Facade/Adapter, API Layer Cake

Purane system ko naye system me badalne ke liye kuch proven patterns hain. Ye patterns risk ko kam karte hain aur migration ko manageable banate hain.

Strangler Fig

Strangler Fig pattern me tum nayi functionality ko naye system me banate ho aur dheere-dheere purane system ko "gala ghont" kar (strangle) replace karte ho. Pehle ek chhota part migrate karo (jaise Attendee), phir doosra, phir teesra. Jab saara migrate ho jaaye, toh purana system hata do. Ye sabse safe migration pattern hai.

Facade and Adapter

  • Facade: Ek naya, simple interface banata hai purane system ke upar. Clients facade se baat karte hain, purane system ki complexity nahi dekhte.
  • Adapter: Ek purane interface ko naye interface me badalta hai taaki do systems jo compatible nahi hain, wo ek-doosre se baat kar sakein.

API Layer Cake

API Layer Cake me tum APIs ko layers me organize karte ho — experience APIs (UI ke liye), process APIs (business logic ke liye), system APIs (data ke liye). Har layer apna kaam karta hai aur neeche wali layer ko use karta hai. Isse APIs ko manage aur evolve karna aasan hota hai.

Pain points aur opportunities

  • Upgrade/maintenance issues: Purana system maintain karna mushkil hai — dependencies outdated hain, koi nahi jaanta kaise kaam karta hai.
  • Performance issues: Monolith slow hai — ek part slow hone se poora system slow ho jaata hai.
  • Highly coupled APIs: APIs ek-doosre se tightly coupled hain — ek badlo toh doosri tootti hai. Inhe decouple karna hai.

Summary (Ch 8): APIs se system evolve karo — clear abstractions aur domain boundaries banao, end-state chuno (monolith/SOA/microservices/functions), fitness functions se architecture ko guard karo, aur Strangler Fig/Facade/API Layer Cake patterns se safely migrate karo.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 8
09.1Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

Cloud migration — 6 Rs strategy

Cloud me jaane ka matlab sirf servers ko cloud par shift karna nahi hai — ye ek strategy hai. Gartner ke 6 Rs batate hain ki har application ke liye kaunsa approach lena hai.

RMatlabKab use karo
Retain / RevisitAbhi cloud me mat jaao — on-premise hi rakho, baad me revisit karoJab application cloud ke liye ready nahi hai ya compliance rokta hai
Rehost ("lift and shift")Application ko jaise hai waise hi cloud me le jaao — koi change nahiJab jaldi migrate karna hai aur code change nahi karna
Replatform ("lift and reshape")Application ko cloud me le jaao aur thode changes karo (jaise managed database use karo)Jab tum cloud ke fayde lena chahte ho bina poora rewrite kiye
RepurchaseApplication ko chhod kar SaaS product kharidoJab koi SaaS product tumhari zaroorat poori karta hai
Refactor / Re-architectApplication ko dobara design karo cloud-native tareeke seJab tumhe cloud ke poore fayde chahiye (scalability, resilience)
RetireApplication ko band kar do — iski zaroorat nahi haiJab application outdated hai ya use nahi hota

Har application ke liye alag R ho sakta hai. Attendee service ke liye Replatform chuna gaya — use cloud me le jaaya gaya aur managed services use ki gayi, bina poora rewrite kiye.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 9
09.2Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

Replatforming case study — Attendee to cloud

Case study me Attendee service ko cloud me replatform kiya gaya. Ye batata hai ki replatforming real me kaise hoti hai — kya badalta hai aur kya same rehta hai.

Figure 9-2. Infrastructure diagram showing extracted API gateway and Attendee service

Replatforming me kya badla

  • Infrastructure: On-premise servers se cloud (Kubernetes) par gaye.
  • Database: Self-managed database se managed database service par gaye.
  • API gateway: Cloud ka managed API gateway use karne lage.
  • Observability: Cloud ke monitoring/logging tools use karne lage.

Replatforming me kya same raha

  • API contract: Attendee API ka contract same raha — consumers ko koi change nahi dikha.
  • Business logic: Attendee ko manage karne ka logic same raha.
  • Code: Zyada code change nahi hua — sirf configuration aur infrastructure badla.

Yehi replatforming ki taakat hai: tum cloud ke fayde lete ho (managed services, scalability, reliability) bina API ya business logic ko tode.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 9
09.3Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

API management aur North–South vs East–West

Jab tum cloud me jaate ho, toh traffic management aur bhi important ho jaata hai. North–south (bahar se andar) aur east–west (service-to-service) traffic ke beech ki line dhundhli hone lagti hai.

Role of API management

API management ka matlab hai APIs ko product ki tarah manage karna — developer portal, documentation, onboarding, analytics, monetization. Cloud me API management aur bhi important ho jaata hai kyunki APIs ki sankhya badhti hai aur consumers alag-alag jagah hote hain.

North–South vs East–West — blurring lines

  • North–south: Bahar se andar aane wala traffic (users → API gateway → services). Ye API gateway handle karta hai.
  • East–west: Services ke beech ka traffic (service → service). Ye service mesh handle karta hai.

Cloud me ye line dhundhli ho jaati hai — ek service jo cloud me hai, wo doosre cloud ya on-premise service se baat kar sakti hai. Isliye tumhe dono (gateway + mesh) ko ek saath sochna padta hai.

Start at the edge and work inward

Cloud migration karte waqt edge se shuru karo aur andar ki taraf jaao. Pehle API gateway ko cloud me le jaao, phir ek-ek karke services ko migrate karo. Isse tum dheere-dheere migrate kar sakte ho bina big-bang ke.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 9
09.4Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

Zonal architecture se Zero Trust tak

Traditional security zonal architecture par based thi — andar safe hai, bahar unsafe hai. Zero Trust kehta hai: kisi par bharosa mat karo, har request ko verify karo — chahe wo andar se aaye ya bahar se.

Getting in the zone — zonal architecture

Zonal architecture me network ko zones me baanta jaata hai (jaise DMZ, internal zone, data zone). Har zone ke beech firewalls hote hain. Ye kaam karta hai jab saara infrastructure ek data center me ho, lekin cloud aur distributed systems me zones ko maintain karna mushkil hai.

Trust no one and verify — Zero Trust

Zero Trust me har request ko verify kiya jaata hai — identity, device, context, aur behavior ke hisaab se. Koi bhi request automatically trusted nahi hoti, chahe wo internal network se aaye. Har service ek-doosre ko authenticate karti hai (mTLS) aur authorize karti hai (policies).

Role of service mesh in Zero Trust

Service mesh Zero Trust ko implement karne me madad karta hai — mTLS se har service ek-doosre ko verify karti hai, aur policies se decide hota hai ki kaunsi service kis se baat kar sakti hai. Mesh ke bina Zero Trust implement karna har service me security code likhne jaisa hai — mushkil aur error-prone.

Summary (Ch 9): Cloud migration ke liye 6 Rs use karo — har app ke liye sahi R chuno. Replatforming se cloud ke fayde lo bina API tode. North–south aur east–west traffic ko ek saath manage karo. Aur security ke liye Zero Trust apnao — kisi par bharosa mat karo, har request verify karo.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 9
10.1Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

Journey recap — Conway's Law aur decision types

Poori book ka safar yahan khatam hota hai. Conference system monolith se shuru hua, Attendee API nikala, gateway lagaya, mesh lagaya, deploy/release seekha, secure kiya, aur ant me cloud me le gaya. Ye journey ek template hai — tum apne system ke liye bhi aisa kar sakte ho.

Figure 10-1. Original conference system architecture

APIs, Conway's Law, aur tumhara organization

Conway's Law kehta hai: organizations aise systems design karte hain jo unki communication structure ko copy karte hain. Agar tumhari teams silos me kaam karti hain, toh tumhara system bhi silos me hoga. Agar tum loosely coupled teams chahte ho, toh pehle teams ko loosely coupled banao — architecture apne aap follow karega. APIs teams ke beech ke contracts hain — wo organization structure ko reflect karte hain.

Understanding decision types

Har decision ek jaisa nahi hota:

  • Reversible decisions: Aasani se wapas liye ja sakte hain (jaise ek library chunna). Inhe jaldi lo — zyada socho mat.
  • Irreversible decisions: Wapas lena mushkil hai (jaise ek database ya cloud provider chunna). Inhe soch-samajh ke lo — ADR (Architecture Decision Records) likho.

Zyada decisions reversible hote hain. Unhe jaldi lo aur aage badho. Irreversible decisions par time lagao.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 10
10.2Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

Future — async, HTTP/3, platform-based mesh

API architecture evolve ho rahi hai. Kuch trends jo aane wale hain, unhe samajhna zaroori hai taaki tum future ke liye taiyaar raho.

Async communication

Synchronous (request/response) ke alawa asynchronous communication (events, messaging) bhi important hai. Jab ek service ko doosri ko turant jawab nahi chahiye, toh events use karo — ye decoupling badhata hai aur resilience deta hai. AsyncAPI OpenAPI jaisa hai lekin events ke liye.

HTTP/3
