HTTP/3 aane wala hai aur ye sab kuch badal dega. HTTP/3 QUIC protocol par based hai (UDP par), jo HTTP/2 se faster hai — khaas taur par lossy networks (mobile) par. HTTP/3 se latency kam hogi aur performance badhegi.

Platform-based mesh

Service mesh platform ka hissa ban raha hai — alag tool nahi, platform ki capability. Future me mesh ko alag se deploy nahi karna padega; wo platform (jaise Kubernetes) me built-in hoga. Isse mesh ko adopt karna aur bhi aasan ho jaayega.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 10
10.3Part IV · Evolutionary Architecture

Keep learning — fundamentals, news, practice

API architecture ek aisa field hai jo hamesha evolve hota rehta hai. Book khatam hone ka matlab ye nahi ki seekhna khatam ho gaya. Yahan bataya gaya hai ki aage kaise seekhte raho.

Continually honing the fundamentals

Fundamentals hamesha kaam aate hain — HTTP, REST, networking, security. Nayi technology aati-jaati rehti hai, lekin fundamentals same rehte hain. Unhe mazboot rakho.

Keeping up-to-date with industry news

Industry news follow karo — blogs, newsletters, conferences. API world me kya naya ho raha hai, ye jaanna zaroori hai taaki tum peeche na reh jaao.

Radars, quadrants, and trend reports

ThoughtWorks Technology Radar, CNCF Landscape, aur aisi reports dekho — ye batati hain ki kaunsi technology adopt karni hai, kaunsi try karni hai, aur kaunsi avoid karni hai.

Learning by doing aur teaching

  • Learning by doing: APIs banao, deploy karo, todho, fix karo. Hands-on karne se sabse zyada seekhte ho.
  • Learning by teaching: Doosron ko sikhaoge toh khud bhi achhi tarah samjhoge. Blog likho, talk do, ya team me share karo.

Book ka aakhri sandesh: APIs sirf technology nahi hain — wo tumhare system ko evolve karne ka tareeka hain. Achhi APIs banao, unhe test karo, secure karo, aur unhe evolve hone do. Aur hamesha seekhte raho.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly, Chapter 10

AttendeesController.java — REST endpoints (GET list, GET one, POST, DELETE)https://github.com/masteringapi/attendees/blob/main/src/main/java/com/masteringapi/attendees/controller/AttendeesController.java
package com.masteringapi.attendees.controller;

import com.masteringapi.attendees.model.Attendee;
import com.masteringapi.attendees.model.AttendeeNotFoundException;
import com.masteringapi.attendees.model.AttendeeResponse;
import com.masteringapi.attendees.service.AttendeeStore;
import io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations.Operation;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.validation.annotation.Validated;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;

import java.net.URI;
import java.util.ArrayList;

@RestController
public class AttendeesController {
    private AttendeeStore store;

    public AttendeesController(@Autowired AttendeeStore store) {
        this.store = store;
    }

    @GetMapping("/attendees")
    @ResponseBody
    @Operation(summary = "Retrieve a list of all attendees registered in the system")
    public AttendeeResponse getAttendees() {
        return new AttendeeResponse(new ArrayList<>(store.getAttendees()));
    }

    @GetMapping("/attendees/{id}")
    @ResponseBody
    @Operation(summary = "Retrieve a specific attendee registered in the system")
    public ResponseEntity<Attendee> getAttendee(@PathVariable(value = "id") Integer id) {
        try {
            return ResponseEntity.ok(this.store.getAttendee(id));
        } catch(AttendeeNotFoundException ex) {
            return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
        }
    }

    @PostMapping("attendees")
    @ResponseBody
    @Operation(summary = "Create a new attendee")
    public ResponseEntity<Void> addAttendee(@Validated @RequestBody Attendee attendee) {
        int id = this.store.addAttendee(attendee);
        URI uri = URI.create("/attendees/" + id);
        return ResponseEntity.created(uri).build();
    }

    @DeleteMapping("/attendees/{id}")
    @ResponseBody
    @Operation(summary = "Delete a specific attendee")
    public ResponseEntity<Attendee> deleteAttendee(@PathVariable(value = "id") Integer id) {
        try {
            this.store.removeAttendee(id);
            return ResponseEntity.ok().build();
        } catch(AttendeeNotFoundException ex) {
            return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
        }
    }

    @PutMapping("attendees/{id}")
    @ResponseBody
    @Operation(summary = "Update an attendees details registered in the system")
    public ResponseEntity<Attendee> updateAttendee(@PathVariable(value = "id") Integer id, @RequestBody Attendee attendee) {
        try {
            this.store.updateAttendee(id, attendee);
            return ResponseEntity.noContent().build();
        } catch(AttendeeNotFoundException ex) {
            return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
        }
    }
}
Attendee.java — model (givenName, surname, email, validation)https://github.com/masteringapi/attendees/blob/main/src/main/java/com/masteringapi/attendees/model/Attendee.java
package com.masteringapi.attendees.model;

import javax.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import javax.validation.constraints.Size;
import java.util.Objects;

public class Attendee {
    private Integer id;

    public Attendee() {

    }

    public Attendee(com.masteringapi.attendees.grpc.server.Attendee attendee) {
        this.surname = attendee.getSurname();
        this.givenName = attendee.getGivenName();
        this.email = attendee.getEmail();
    }

    @NotNull
    @Size(max=35)
    private String givenName;

    @NotNull
    @Size(max=35)
    private String surname;

    @NotNull
    @Size(max=254)
    private String email;

    public Integer getId() {
        return id;
    }

    public void setId(Integer id) {
        this.id = id;
    }

    public String getGivenName() {
        return givenName;
    }

    public void setGivenName(String givenName) {
        this.givenName = givenName;
    }

    public String getSurname() {
        return surname;
    }

    public void setSurname(String surname) {
        this.surname = surname;
    }

    public String getEmail() {
        return email;
    }

    public void setEmail(String email) {
        this.email = email;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
        Attendee attendee = (Attendee) o;
        return Objects.equals(id, attendee.id);
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(id);
    }
}
AttendeeStore.java — in-memory store (mock data, [Name] placeholders)https://github.com/masteringapi/attendees/blob/main/src/main/java/com/masteringapi/attendees/service/AttendeeStore.java
package com.masteringapi.attendees.service;

import com.masteringapi.attendees.model.Attendee;
import com.masteringapi.attendees.model.AttendeeNotFoundException;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

@Component
public class AttendeeStore {
    private final Map<Integer, Attendee> attendees = new LinkedHashMap<>();

    private final AtomicInteger counter = new AtomicInteger(0);

    public AttendeeStore() {
        //Setup some mock data
        Attendee attendee = new Attendee();
        attendee.setId(counter.incrementAndGet());
        attendee.setGivenName("[Name]");
        attendee.setSurname("[Name]");
        attendee.setEmail("[Name]@example.com");
        this.attendees.put(1, attendee);
        attendee = new Attendee();
        attendee.setId(counter.incrementAndGet());
        attendee.setGivenName("[Name]");
        attendee.setSurname("[Name]");
        attendee.setEmail("[Name]@example.com");
        this.attendees.put(2, attendee);
        attendee = new Attendee();
        attendee.setId(counter.incrementAndGet());
        attendee.setGivenName("[Name]");
        attendee.setSurname("[Name]");
        attendee.setEmail("[Name]@example.com");
        this.attendees.put(3, attendee);
    }

    public Collection<Attendee> getAttendees() {
        return this.attendees.values();
    }

    public Attendee getAttendee(Integer id) throws AttendeeNotFoundException {
        if(this.attendees.containsKey(id)) {
            return this.attendees.get(id);
        } else {
            throw new AttendeeNotFoundException();
        }
    }

    public int addAttendee(Attendee attendee) {
        int id = counter.incrementAndGet();
        attendee.setId(id);
        this.attendees.put(id, attendee);
        return this.attendees.size();
    }

    public void removeAttendee(Integer id) throws AttendeeNotFoundException {
        if(this.attendees.containsKey(id)) {
            this.attendees.remove(id);
        } else {
            throw new AttendeeNotFoundException();
        }
    }

    public void updateAttendee(Integer id, Attendee attendee) throws AttendeeNotFoundException {
        if(this.attendees.containsKey(id)) {
            attendee.setId(id);
            this.attendees.put(id, attendee);
        } else {
            throw new AttendeeNotFoundException();
        }
    }
}
AttendeesServiceImpl.java — gRPC service implementationhttps://github.com/masteringapi/attendees/blob/main/src/main/java/com/masteringapi/attendees/grpc/AttendeesServiceImpl.java
package com.masteringapi.attendees.grpc;

import com.google.rpc.Code;
import com.google.rpc.Status;
import com.masteringapi.attendees.grpc.server.*;
import com.masteringapi.attendees.model.AttendeeNotFoundException;
import com.masteringapi.attendees.service.AttendeeStore;
import io.grpc.protobuf.StatusProto;
import io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver;
import net.devh.boot.grpc.server.service.GrpcService;
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;

@GrpcService
public class AttendeesServiceImpl extends AttendeesServiceGrpc.AttendeesServiceImplBase {

    private final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(AttendeesServiceImpl.class);

    private final AttendeeStore store;

    public AttendeesServiceImpl(@Autowired AttendeeStore store) {
        this.store = store;
    }

    @Override
    public void getAttendees(GetAttendeesRequest request, StreamObserver<GetAttendeesResponse> responseObserver) {
        GetAttendeesResponse.Builder responseBuilder = com.masteringapi.attendees.grpc.server.GetAttendeesResponse.newBuilder();

        for(com.masteringapi.attendees.model.Attendee attendee: store.getAttendees()) {
            Attendee grpcAttendee = Attendee.newBuilder()
                    .setId(attendee.getId())
                    .setGivenName(attendee.getGivenName())
                    .setSurname(attendee.getSurname())
                    .setEmail(attendee.getEmail())
                    .build();
            responseBuilder.addAttendees(grpcAttendee);
        }

        responseObserver.onNext(responseBuilder.build());
        responseObserver.onCompleted();
    }

    @Override
    public void createAttendee(CreateAttendeeRequest request, StreamObserver<CreateAttendeeResponse> responseObserver) {
        CreateAttendeeResponse.Builder responseBuilder = CreateAttendeeResponse.newBuilder();

        int id = this.store.addAttendee(new com.masteringapi.attendees.model.Attendee(request.getAttendee()));

        Attendee attendee = Attendee.newBuilder().mergeFrom(request.getAttendee())
                .setId(id)
                .build();
        responseBuilder.setAttendee(attendee);
        responseObserver.onNext(responseBuilder.build());
        responseObserver.onCompleted();
    }

    @Override
    public void getAttendee(GetAttendeeRequest request, StreamObserver<GetAttendeeResponse> responseObserver) {
        GetAttendeeResponse.Builder responseBuilder = GetAttendeeResponse.newBuilder();

        try {
            com.masteringapi.attendees.model.Attendee attendee = this.store.getAttendee(request.getId());
            Attendee grpcAttendee = Attendee.newBuilder()
                    .setId(attendee.getId())
                    .setGivenName(attendee.getGivenName())
                    .setSurname(attendee.getSurname())
                    .setEmail(attendee.getEmail())
                    .build();
            responseBuilder.setAttendee(grpcAttendee);
            responseObserver.onNext(responseBuilder.build());
            responseObserver.onCompleted();
        } catch (AttendeeNotFoundException e) {
            Status status = Status.newBuilder().setCode(Code.NOT_FOUND.getNumber())
                            .setMessage("Attendee Not Found")
                                    .build();
            responseObserver.onError(StatusProto.toStatusRuntimeException(status));
            logger.error("Could not find attendee", e);
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void deleteAttendee(DeleteAttendeeRequest request, StreamObserver<DeleteAttendeeResponse> responseObserver) {
        DeleteAttendeeResponse.Builder responseBuilder = DeleteAttendeeResponse.newBuilder();

        try {
            this.store.removeAttendee(request.getId());
            responseObserver.onNext(responseBuilder.build());
            responseObserver.onCompleted();
        } catch (AttendeeNotFoundException e) {
            Status status = Status.newBuilder().setCode(Code.NOT_FOUND.getNumber())
                    .setMessage("Attendee Not Found")
                    .build();
            responseObserver.onError(StatusProto.toStatusRuntimeException(status));
            logger.error("Could not find attendee to delete", e);
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void updateAttendee(UpdateAttendeeRequest request, StreamObserver<UpdateAttendeeResponse> responseObserver) {
        UpdateAttendeeResponse.Builder responseBuilder = UpdateAttendeeResponse.newBuilder();

        try {
            this.store.updateAttendee(request.getAttendee().getId(),
                    new com.masteringapi.attendees.model.Attendee(request.getAttendee()));

            responseBuilder.setAttendee(request.getAttendee());
            responseObserver.onNext(responseBuilder.build());
            responseObserver.onCompleted();
        } catch (AttendeeNotFoundException e) {
            Status status = Status.newBuilder().setCode(Code.NOT_FOUND.getNumber())
                    .setMessage("Attendee Not Found")
                    .build();
            responseObserver.onError(StatusProto.toStatusRuntimeException(status));
            logger.error("Unable to update attendee", e);
        }
    }
}

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: rollouts-demo
spec:
  replicas: 5
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
        - setWeight: 20
        - pause: {}
        - setWeight: 40
        - pause: {duration: 10}
        - setWeight: 60
        - pause: {duration: 10}
        - setWeight: 80
        - pause: {duration: 10}
  revisionHistoryLimit: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: attendees-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: attendees-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: attendees
          image: jpgough/attendees:v1
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
              protocol: TCP
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: 32Mi
              cpu: 5m

F1End Matter

Interview FAQs

Interview me API architecture se poochhe jaane wale sawaal — har ek ka jawab Hinglish me, book ke concepts ke saath.

1. API design karte waqt sabse pehle kya sochna chahiye?

Consumer ko samjho — kaun use karega, use kya chahiye, aur wo kis tarah integrate karega. Technology (REST/RPC/GraphQL) baad me chuno, pehle consumer ki zaroorat samjho. Book me CFP team aur legacy team ke alag-alag needs se yehi sikhaya gaya hai.

2. REST aur RPC me main farak kya hai?

REST ek resource model dikhata hai aur stateless hota hai (har request independent). RPC ek method ko directly expose karta hai aur state implementation par depend karta hai. REST external consumers ke liye behtar hai (loose coupling), RPC internal high-performance service-to-service calls ke liye behtar hai (gRPC).

3. Richardson Maturity Model ke levels kya hain?

Level 0: HTTP/RPC (ek URI, koi resource model nahi). Level 1: Resources (har resource ki identity hai). Level 2: Verbs (sahi HTTP methods — GET/PUT/DELETE). Level 3: Hypermedia/HATEOAS (response me aage ke actions ke links). Level 2 aksar practical target hai; Level 3 har jagah zaroori nahi.

4. GraphQL kab use karna chahiye?

Jab client ko kayi sources se exact fields chahiye hon (jaise mobile apps, reporting systems), ya jab ek single version saari APIs par chahiye ho. GraphQL REST/RPC ki jagah nahi leta — ye unke upar ek query layer hai.

5. PII ko URL me kyun nahi daalna chahiye?

Kyunki URL paths aur query parameters galti se cache ho sakte hain — server logs, browser history, network logs me. Isliye email jaise PII ko URL me mat daalo; opaque ID use karo (jaise /attendees/1). Microsoft guidelines section 7.9 me yehi kaha gaya hai.

6. Pagination pehle se kyun rakhni chahiye?

Kyunki baad me raw array se object (with @nextLink) me badalna breaking change hai. Pehle se array ko object me nest karo ({value: [...], @nextLink: ...}) taaki baad me pagination add kar sakein bina compatibility tode.

7. OpenAPI Specification kya hai aur kyun zaroori hai?

OAS ek JSON/YAML representation hai jo API ki structure, domain objects, aur security ko describe karta hai. Isse code generate kar sakte ho (client + server stubs), request/response validate kar sakte ho, aur consumers ko API samajhna aasan hota hai. Swagger iska original implementation tha.

8. API versioning kaise karein?

Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) use karo. Breaking changes (naam badalna, field hatana) se bacho; naye fields backward-compatible tareeke se add karo. Versioning strategy pehle se decide karo taaki consumers ko pata ho kya expect karein.

9. Contract testing kya hai aur ye schema validation se alag kaise hai?

Contract ek agreement hai consumer aur producer ke beech — 'agar tum aisi request karoge, toh main aisa response dunga'. Schema batata hai ki system compatible hai ya nahi; contract ek defined interaction hai jisme examples hote hain. Contract se stub server aur tests generate hote hain, jo decoupling deta hai.

10. Producer contracts vs consumer-driven contracts (CDC) — kab kya?

Producer contracts jab API external third parties ke liye hai (jaise Microsoft Graph API) — producer khud contracts define karta hai. CDC jab consumer aur producer ek hi org me hain — consumer batata hai use kya chahiye, discussion hoti hai, phir agree karte hain. CDC me discussion se value milti hai.

11. Test Quadrant aur Test Pyramid me farak kya hai?

Test Quadrant batata hai kaunse tests chahiye (Q1 unit/component, Q2 business, Q3 functional/exploratory, Q4 technical). Test Pyramid batata hai kitne tests chahiye (zyada unit, beech me service, kam E2E). Dono ko ek saath use karo.

12. Ice cream cone kya hai aur ye galat kyun hai?

Ice cream cone pyramid ka ulta hai — zyada E2E tests, kam unit tests. Ye false sense of security deta hai kyunki E2E tests slow aur flaky hote hain aur fail hone par pata nahi chalta ki problem kahan hai. Pyramid follow karo: zyada unit, kam E2E.

13. API gateway aur load balancer me farak kya hai?

Load balancer sirf traffic ko distribute karta hai (health checks ke saath). API gateway usse zyada hai — routing + auth + rate limiting + observability + lifecycle + developer portal. Sirf traffic distribute karna hai toh load balancer kaafi hai; APIs ko product ki tarah manage karna hai toh gateway lo.

14. API gateway ko ESB ki tarah kyun nahi use karna chahiye?

Kyunki gateway ka kaam edge par traffic manage karna hai, business logic ya heavy transformation karna nahi. Agar gateway me business logic daal doge, toh wo ESB ban jaayega aur wahi purani problems (tight coupling, complexity) wapas aa jaayengi.

15. Service mesh kya hai aur ye API gateway se alag kaise hai?

Service mesh service-to-service (east–west) traffic manage karta hai — sidecar proxies ke through routing, observability, security. API gateway ingress (north–south) traffic manage karta hai. Dono ko alag rakho — gateway ko mesh ki jagah aur mesh ko gateway ki jagah use mat karo.

16. Sidecar proxy kya hai?

Sidecar ek proxy container hai jo har service instance ke saath chalta hai. Application code seedha doosri service ko call nahi karta — wo sidecar ko call karta hai, aur sidecar request ko route karta hai, security enforce karta hai, aur telemetry emit karta hai. Application code ko ye sab pata bhi nahi chalta.

17. Service mesh kab use karna chahiye aur kab nahi?

Mesh use karo jab kayi languages hon, advanced features (auth, rate limiting, observability) chahiye hon, ya consumers/providers badh rahe hon. Library kaafi hai jab single language ho aur sirf simple routing chahiye ho. Mesh free lunch nahi hai — iski complexity aur operational cost bhi hai.

18. mTLS kya hai?

mTLS (mutual TLS) me dono taraf (client aur server) ek-doosre ko verify karte hain certificates se. Normal TLS me sirf server verify hota hai; mTLS me dono verify hote hain. Service mesh mTLS enforce karta hai taaki services ek-doosre ki identity verify kar sakein.

19. Deployment aur release me farak kya hai?

Deployment ka matlab hai code ko production me daalna; release ka matlab hai users ko feature dikhana. Feature flags se dono ko alag kar sakte ho — code deploy karo feature off ke saath, phir flag on karke release karo. Isse rollback aasan hota hai.

20. Feature flags ka sabse bada risk kya hai?

Flags ko saaf na karna. Knight Capital ne ek feature flag reuse kiya aur failed deployment ke saath $460 million ka loss hua. Flags ko unique naam do aur kaam khatam hone par poori tarah hata do.

21. Canary, blue-green, aur traffic mirroring me farak kya hai?

Canary: naye version ko chhote % users ko do, dheere-dheere badhao. Blue-green: do environments rakho, traffic ko ek saath switch karo (rollback instant). Mirroring: real traffic ki copy naye version par bhejo, response purane se lo (users affect nahi hote).

22. Observability ke three pillars kya hain?

Metrics (numbers — request rate, error rate, latency), Logs (events ka record), Traces (ek request ka poora journey). Teeno ko ek saath use karo — metrics se trends dekho, logs se debug karo, traces se bottlenecks dhoondho.

23. Threat modeling kya hai aur STRIDE kya hai?

Threat modeling wo process hai jisse tum pehle se soch lete ho ki system par kya attacks ho sakte hain. STRIDE 6 categories hai: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege. Har category ek type ke attack ko represent karti hai.

24. Rate limiting aur load shedding me farak kya hai?

Rate limiting: ek consumer kitne requests bhej sakta hai, use limit karo (429 return karo). Load shedding: jab system overload ho, toh kuch requests ko jaan-bujh kar drop kar do taaki system poori tarah down na ho aur critical requests serve ho sakein.

25. Authentication aur authorization me farak kya hai?

Authentication: tum kaun ho? (identity verify karna). Authorization: tum kya kar sakte ho? (permissions check karna). Dono alag hain — pehle authenticate karo, phir authorize karo.

26. OAuth2 kya hai aur JWT kya hai?

OAuth2 ek authorization framework hai jo third-party apps ko limited access deta hai bina password share kiye. JWT (JSON Web Token) ek token format hai jo claims carry karta hai. JWT ko JWS se sign karte hain (integrity) ya JWE se encrypt karte hain (confidentiality).

27. Authorization Code Grant + PKCE kya hai?

Authorization Code Grant me user login karta hai, code milta hai, phir code ko token se exchange karte hain. PKCE iska extension hai jo mobile/native apps ke liye hai — code verifier/challenge se verify hota hai ki wahi client hai. Public clients ke liye PKCE use karna chahiye.

28. Client Credentials Grant kab use hota hai?

Jab ek system doosre system se baat karta hai aur koi user involved nahi hai (system-to-system). Client apni ID aur secret se directly token leta hai. Ye user login ke liye nahi hai.

29. OIDC aur SAML me farak kya hai?

OIDC (OpenID Connect) OAuth2 ke upar identity layer hai — JSON-based, mobile-friendly, aaj ka standard. SAML 2.0 purana XML-based standard hai jo enterprise SSO ke liye use hota hai. Dono user identity verify karte hain, lekin OIDC modern hai.

30. API keys aur user tokens ko mix kyun nahi karna chahiye?

API keys long-lived hote hain aur inme user context nahi hota — ye system-to-system ke liye hain. User tokens short-lived hote hain aur user ki identity/permissions carry karte hain. Mix karne se pata nahi chalta ki kaunsa user request kar raha hai aur key leak hone par revoke karna mushkil hota hai.

31. Zero Trust kya hai?

Zero Trust kehta hai: kisi par bharosa mat karo, har request ko verify karo — chahe wo andar se aaye ya bahar se. Traditional zonal architecture me andar safe mana jaata tha; Zero Trust me har request identity, device, context ke hisaab se verify hoti hai. Service mesh (mTLS + policies) Zero Trust implement karne me madad karta hai.

32. Strangler Fig pattern kya hai?

Purane system ko dheere-dheere replace karne ka pattern. Nayi functionality ko naye system me banao aur ek-ek karke purane system ke parts ko migrate karo. Jab saara migrate ho jaaye, toh purana system hata do. Ye sabse safe migration pattern hai.

33. Fitness functions kya hain?

Fitness functions automated checks hain jo batate hain ki architecture goals ko meet kar raha hai ya nahi. Jaise 'koi service doosri service ke database ko directly access nahi kar sakti'. Inhe CI/CD me run karo taaki violations jaldi pakde jaayein.

34. Conway's Law kya hai?

Conway's Law kehta hai: organizations aise systems design karte hain jo unki communication structure ko copy karte hain. Agar teams silos me hain, toh system bhi silos me hoga. Loosely coupled teams chahte ho toh pehle teams ko loosely coupled banao.

35. Cloud migration ke 6 Rs kya hain?

Retain/Revisit (abhi mat jaao), Rehost (lift and shift), Replatform (lift and reshape), Repurchase (SaaS kharido), Refactor/Re-architect (dobara design karo), Retire (band kar do). Har application ke liye alag R ho sakta hai.

36. API gateway aur service mesh ko ek saath kaise use karein?

Gateway ingress (north–south) ke liye — bahar se aane wala traffic. Mesh service-to-service (east–west) ke liye — internal traffic. Dono ko alag rakho aur ek saath use karo — gateway request ko andar laata hai, mesh use services ke beech route karta hai.

SOURCESource: Mastering API Architecture, O’Reilly (FAQs based on the book’s concepts)
